title: Developer experience docs: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, site ops & canonical fixes (Playbook)
author: Samira Khan
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook defines the standards, templates, and canonical fixes for all Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation related to SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and top support issues. It is intended for docs authors, SDK maintainers, developer advocates, and support engineers.

Scope
- SDK reference guides and idiomatic examples (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Java).
- Quickstarts and repo templates for common patterns (chat, instruction-following generation, embeddings, re-ranking).
- Canonical API examples for the public docs site and internal troubleshooting KB.
- Docs site operating procedures: publish, review, CI, and rollback steps.
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage-first remediation steps).

Audience
- DevEx writers & maintainers
- SDK engineering teams
- Support & SRE on-call engineers

Document structure (how to use this page)
1) Author the SDK guide or quickstart using the templates below.
2) Add the doc to the docs site PR and run docs-site CI checks.
3) Follow the publish checklist.
4) If the issue is reported by Support, consult the Top Support Issues section for canonical fixes.

---

Standards for SDK Guides

Overview & goals
Every SDK guide must: be short, language-idiomatic, contain an authorization example, show sync/async usage where applicable, include at least one end-to-end quickstart, and contain a troubleshooting section with common errors.

Required sections (order matters)
- Short intro (1-3 paragraphs) describing intent and target audience.
- Quickstart (copy-paste runnable).
- API reference links (canonical model names and options).
- Advanced patterns (streaming, function/tool-calling, batching).
- Troubleshooting & top error codes.
- Test matrix and supported SDK versions.

Code style & snippets
- Use triple-backtick fenced blocks and annotate language (```python, ```bash, ```js).
- Keep examples <= 40 lines; focus on a single task per snippet.
- Prefer environment variables for API keys: REDWOOD_API_KEY.

Example (Python quickstart)
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
resp = client.text.generate(model="redwood-alpha-1", prompt="Write a 2-sentence product blurb")
print(resp.text)
```

Quickstarts & Templates (repo-ready)

Canonical quickstarts to maintain (each must be a small repo template)
- quickstart-text-gen (Python + Dockerfile + README)
- quickstart-chat-app (Node/Next.js + streaming server example)
- quickstart-embeddings-search (Go + minimal vector store example)
- quickstart-batch-inference (Python + worker + batching config)

Quickstart template checklist
1. README with objectives and time-to-complete.
2. Dockerfile + devcontainer (optional).
3. CI job that runs lint and smoke tests (e.g., run a single request using a demo key).
4. LICENSE (Apache-2.0) and CONTRIBUTING.md.

Template README skeleton
- Title
- What you will build
- Prereqs (node/python/docker)
- Quick start (copy/paste commands)
- How it works (brief architecture)
- Next steps & production notes

API Examples (canonical snippets for docs site)

Text generation (curl)
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"Summarize the following: <text>","max_tokens":120}'
```

Streaming chat (Node)
```js
import { RedwoodClient } from "@redwood/inference"
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: "redwood-chat-1", messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Explain HTTP caching" }] })
for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk.delta) }
```

Embedding + search (pseudo-CLI)
```
# 1) create embedding 2) persist vector 3) query top-k by cosine
EMBED_PAYLOAD='{"model":"emb-small-1","input":"How to optimize inference"}'
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d "$EMBED_PAYLOAD"
```

Docs site operating procedures (publish & rollback)

Pre-publish checklist (author)
- Link to related pages and API reference.
- Add labels and reviewers in page metadata.
- Include smoke tests in PR that exercise at least one example.
- Validate code blocks with docs site linter (./scripts/lint-code-blocks).
- Confirm sample API keys are redacted.

Docs CI steps (automated)
1. Run markdown lint and spellcheck.
2. Run code-block syntax check and snippet execution (where marked runnable).
3. Build site and run visual regression tests for critical pages.
4. Deploy to staging site under /staging/docs.
5. Automated link-checker runs; broken links block merge.

Publish procedure (for non-critical pages)
1. Merge PR to main -> CI deploys to staging.
2. Wait 24 hrs for review feedback (unless urgent).
3. Approve and tag release; CI deploys to production.

Emergency rollback
- Trigger docs rollback job in CircleCI (job: docs/rollback) which reverts last prod commit and redeploys.
- Post-rollback: open a retro ticket and notify #dev-docs.

Top support issues & canonical fixes (high impact)

1) 401 / Invalid API key (most common)
Symptoms: "401 Unauthorized" or "Invalid API key" in SDK logs.
Canonical fix:
- Confirm env var REDWOOD_API_KEY is set in environment the process runs in.
- Check that the key has not expired or been rotated in the Console.
- For hosted customers: verify account status and quota in Console -> Usage.
- Support KB command to repro: `curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/status`
Ownership: Support -> triage; DevEx docs owner updates quickstart if pattern reappears.

2) Streaming responses truncated / incomplete tokens
Symptoms: stream closes early, or trailing tokens missing.
Canonical fix:
- Confirm client correctly consumes the streaming protocol: do not close connection on first data event.
- Ensure WebSocket/HTTP2 proxies do not buffer or terminate idle streams (AWS ALB default timeout: 60s).
- Suggest enabling keepalive/ping for long-running streams.
- If proxied by Redwood gateway (private deployments), check gateway logs: `gateway/stream-timeout-ms` setting.
Ownership: Eng-serving-runtime + DevEx.

3) High token costs for embeddings/search
Symptoms: unusually large embedding vectors or repeated re-embedding of same inputs.
Canonical fix:
- Verify client uses sentence-level deduplication and caching.
- Use the recommended `emb-small-1` for semantic search; only use `emb-large-1` for high-precision tasks.
- Implement vector caching layer with TTL 7-30 days depending on dataset churn.
Ownership: Product/Eng-DevEx.

4) SDK version mismatch / type errors (JS/TS)
Symptoms: TypeScript compile errors after SDK bump.
Canonical fix:
- Pin SDK minor version in templates (e.g., "@redwood/inference": "^2.3.1").
- Add migration notes in the SDK CHANGELOG and docs site migration guide.
- Provide a code-mod snippet for common API signature changes.
Ownership: SDK team + DevEx.

Support triage play (1st 10 minutes)
1. Reproduce with curl and minimal SDK snippet.
2. Capture request id from client logs (X-Request-ID / X-Trace-Id).
3. Check SRE logs & tracing for the request id.
4. If fix is config change (timeout, key), apply change in sandbox, ask customer to validate.

Publishing & ownership
- Owners: DevEx docs lead (Samira Khan), SDK owners per language listed in language-owners.csv (repo).
- SLA for critical doc fixes: 72 hours from report to published fix (patch).

Checklist before closing a support KB into canonical fix
- Repro steps documented.
- One-line canonical fix and 3-step remediation.
- Add cross-link to impacted SDK guides and quickstarts.
- Add automated smoke test to quickstart repo if feasible.

Appendix: sample configuration table (for quickstarts)
| key | recommended value | rationale |
| REDWOOD_API_KEY | set in env/secret manager | avoids accidental commits |
| REDWOOD_MODEL | redwood-chat-1 | default conversation model |
| BATCH_MAX_TOKENS | 4096 | default batch token limit for batching worker |

Contact & escalation
- Primary docs channel: #dev-docs on Slack.
- Urgent support-email: support@redwood.ai (internal routing).
- For production incidents that involve docs (e.g., misleading sample code), page on-call SRE and notify #dev-docs.

Related artifacts / templates
- Repo templates: /repos/quickstarts/* (dev-ex team).
- Docs linter & snippet runner: /tools/docs-lint/
- SDK release checklist: /eng-developer-experience/sdk-release-checklist.md

Last updated notes
- 2026-12-01: Added streaming troubleshooting guidance and keepalive recommendations (Ethan Park).
- 2026-11-15: Initial playbook created (Samira Khan).

End of document
